angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 619,173 km at 201.72 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 4.9573 +/- 0.0110 mas (same row, RUWE 0.97): 201.72 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.89 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Guenther et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-4427 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...54G/abstract): 619,173 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.9 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Guenther et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-4427 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...54G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5347 +/- 135 K from Guenther et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4427 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...54G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Guenther et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4427 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...54G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-4427.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.494, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
